THE_KEY_DIAGNOSTIC_DETAIL.observation: pi_B3@t100k scores 0.7422 on POLE A -- nearly as high as pi_A3 itself (0.8359), and far higher than pi_B3's FINAL checkpoint scored on Pole A in the corrected crossover (0.5391).
THE_KEY_DIAGNOSTIC_DETAIL.reading: t100k is not a Pole-B specialist that happens to be fairly evaluated. It is an early-training checkpoint that has not yet DIFFERENTIATED at all -- it performs competently and fairly uniformly against BOTH poles, exactly the 'insufficiently differentiated' failure mode this entire research program studies. Its apparently strong delta_B in the trajectory run was measured against only ONE reference (frozen pi_A3 on Pole B) and never checked against Pole A, so the trajectory could not see that t100k's Pole-B competence came bundled with equal Pole-A competence -- i.e. no specialization gap at all, just general strength that happened to land favourably against a single comparator on a single pole on that particular exploratory seed draw.
THE_KEY_DIAGNOSTIC_DETAIL.this_is_exactly_the_risk_the_PI_named_be: 'B100k could be excellent on B but accidentally also strong on A, which would shrink delta_A.' Confirmed directly: delta_A fell from the corrected-crossover final-checkpoint's +0.273 to +0.094 specifically because pi_B3@t100k's Pole-A win rate (0.7422) is so much higher than pi_B3_final's (0.5391).
